thought: Found the defect. Cart.subtotal() at pyshop/cart.py:54 uses `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)`, which iterates only the first N-1 line items and silently skips the last one. With items [mug x2 ($25.00), lamp ($39.99), pen x3 ($3.00)] it sums only mug+lamp = $64.99 and drops the $3.00 pen line, exactly matching the reported wrong value; the correct sum is $67.99 (no bulk discounts apply at these quantities: tiers start at 10+ units per README). LineItem.total and order_total are otherwise consistent with the docs; the off-by-one is the sole cause. No further reads needed.

payload.root_cause: Off-by-one loop in Cart.subtotal() (pyshop/cart.py:52-56): it iterates `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)`, so the last LineItem in self.items is never added to the total. With the cart holding three lines — 2 mugs ($25.00), 1 lamp ($39.99), 3 pens ($3.00) — the pen line is skipped, yielding $64.99 instead of $67.99. Any cart whose most recently appended line is not merged into an existing SKU is undercharged by that line's full (bulk-discounted) amount.
evidence: pyshop/cart.py:52-56 — `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1): total += self.items[i].total` skips the final element of self.items.
pyshop/cart.py:41-43 — new SKUs are appended at the end of self.items, so a distinct product added last is the one dropped.
Reproduces the report exactly: mug line 2×12.50=25.00 + lamp 39.99 = 64.99 (pens line 3×1.00=3.00 excluded); expected 67.99 per tests/test_cart.py:21-25.
pyshop/cart.py:22-25 LineItem.total applies only bulk tiers (10+/50+/100+ per README), none triggered at qtys 2/1/3, so no discount explains the $3.00 shortfall.
